title: Roadmap ships a false claim: "Open Beta — 10 worlds, 11 Guardians, playable free" marked as NOW
evidence:
Phase 02 · Now
Open Beta
10 worlds, 11 Guardians, playable free.
(line 1419) — and line 1418: "Alpha … The core world & first Guardians."
why: This is the single explicit statement of scope on the whole page, it is flagged as the CURRENT phase, and it is false by a factor of ten. Open Beta

Launch
Every device. The full descent.

title: The whole page is invisible if JavaScript fails — and there is a live crash path that makes it fail
evidence: Line 2: `<html lang="en" class="js">` (the `js` class is hard-coded, not added by script). Line 356: `html.js .reveal{opacity:0;transform:translateY(24px);...}`. Every headline, pillar, roadmap node, CTA and the footer disclaimer carries `class="reveal"`, including the hero copy at line 1209. There is no `<noscript>` anywhere in the file. Line 1591, inside the install IIFE that runs before the reveal IIFE, calls `localStorage.getItem('cq_installed')==='1'` with NO try/catch — while the very same file wraps identical calls at lines 1645-1646 in `try{}catch(e){}`.
why: `installed()` is invoked synchronously at lines 1604 and 1610. In Safari Private Browsing, in a locked-down enterprise profile, or with site data blocked, `localStorage.getItem` throws a SecurityError, which aborts the outer IIFE at line 1519 before the reveal observer at line 1677 ever runs — leaving every element with `opacity:0` forever. The real throw path is storage being blocked outright (Chrome \"block all cookies\", Firefox strict/enterprise policy, partitioned third-party contexts), a narrower audience than claimed. (b) The finding missed an existing partial mitigation: website/index.html:480, inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce), already declares html.js .reveal{opacity:1;transform:none;transition:none} — reduced-motion visitors never see the blank page. title: Missing security headers: the _headers file lives outside the deploy directory, and as written it would break the game embed
evidence: `_headers` and `netlify.toml` sit at the repo ROOT; the Cloudflare Pages output directory is `website/`, which contains no `_headers` file (`ls website/_headers` → No such file). Measured production headers carry only x-content-type-options, referrer-policy and `access-control-allow-origin: *`. The root file's own comment (lines 4-8) states Cloudflare "reads this file instead" — but it is not in the published tree. First, no headers ship at all: with no X-Frame-Options and `access-control-allow-origin: *`, any third-party site can iframe playchartquest.com whole and present it as their own product — the concrete risk for a trading-education brand aimed at children is a scam or signal-selling site framing the game to borrow its credibility, with a fake deposit overlay on top. Second, the obvious fix is a trap: `X-Frame-Options: DENY` and `frame-ancestors 'none'` block SAME-ORIGIN framing too, so copying this file as-is would break the site's own hero conversion path — index.html line 2010 iframes `play.html`, and play.html line 71 iframes `game.html`. `font-src 'self'` would simultaneously kill the Google Fonts at index.html line 64.

Then verify in production that the "Enter the Chart" embed still loads before announcing the beta.

The "fix is a trap" half is also correct: index.html:1356 carries `data-game="play.html"` and the JS at 2006-2011 builds an iframe with that src, and play.html:71 is `<iframe id="cqGame">` fed `game.html` at line 108 — two levels of SAME-ORIGIN framing that `DENY` and `frame-ancestors 'none'` both block. index.html:64 is indeed the fonts.googleapis.com stylesheet. verdict.correction: Severity should be P2, not P1: nothing on the live site is broken today and missing headers cost zero beta signups or survey completions under the stated rubric — this is ops/security debt with a booby-trapped fix, not a conversion defect. title: Service worker pins every static asset cache-first forever — a forgotten version bump ships a stale beta to testers

why: The game document itself is safe, which is the big one — but for a beta where fixes ship daily, every non-game asset is frozen. Re-cut a boss portrait, fix a bug in site.js, change `gameUrl` in config.js, or swap the logo, and returning testers keep the old bytes indefinitely. Belt-and-braces: add a `cq.sh` release step that fails the build if `CACHE` in sw.js was not bumped when anything under `website/assets/`, `website/finn/` or `website/bosses/` changed.

why: Second by second on a mid-range phone at ~700 KB/s: t=0 tap Play; t≈0.15 s the 308 lands; t≈0.4 s play.html HTML; t≈0.8 s site.css + config.js clear the render block; t≈0.9 s the iframe src is finally assigned; t≈0.9-4 s game.html (~600 KB compressed) plus supabase plus the 1.87 MB logo stream in; t≈4-7 s the browser parses and executes 1.86 MB of single-file HTML+JS with no progressive render. Nearly a full second of that is pure orchestration overhead before a single game byte is requested. The homepage Enter path is worse — it pays play.html's cost twice-nested and shows the tester a redundant chrome bar inside the embed.
recommendation: (1) Inline the ~1 KB of CSS play.html actually uses and delete the `site.css` link, and inline the single `gameUrl` value instead of blocking on config.js — the iframe src should be assignable from the HTML itself. (2) Better: put `src="game.html"` directly on the `<iframe>` at play.html:76 so the preload scanner starts the game download during play.html's own parse (keep the query-forwarding by having the server or a tiny inline snippet append it). (3) Point index.html:1356 `data-game` at `game.html`, not `play.html`, so the homepage embed stops nesting a second play-bar. (4) Add `<link rel="preconnect">`/`<link rel="prefetch" as="document" href="game.html">` on index.html so the game starts downloading while the tester is still reading the hero.

verdict.reason: Every cited line checks out in source. play.html:16-17 does load assets/site.css (25,507 bytes, verified by ls) as a render-blocking stylesheet and assets/config.js as a render-blocking script with no defer, for a page that is a 52px bar plus an iframe. The iframe at play.html:71 ships with NO src attribute at all — it is only assigned at play.html:108 from inline JS that reads window.CHARTQUEST_CONFIG, so the game document genuinely cannot be requested until play.html's HTML, CSS and config.js have all landed. sw.js lines 4-5 do document the Cloudflare 308 (/play.html -> /play). index.html:1356 does carry data-game="play.html", and index.html:1993-2011 creates an iframe with f.src=src, so the homepage Enter button really does nest play.html (and its fixed 52px .play-bar, plus a "ChartQuest" home link that would load the homepage inside the iframe) inside the 16:10 .game-mount at index.html:691. I grepped play.html and assets/site.js for window.top / self!==top / frameElement — there is no in-iframe detection anywhere, so nothing hides that bar in the embed. The payload numbers are also right: game.html is 1,861,115 bytes and logo.png (referenced at game.html:1195) is 1,871,495 bytes. I could not refute it.
verdict.correction:
Four corrections, none fatal to the finding:

(1) MITIGATION THE FINDING MISSED — sw.js:11-16 precaches './assets/site.css', './assets/site.js', './assets/config.js', and the fetch handler (sw.js:65-70) serves static assets cache-first. So for a repeat visitor with the SW installed, the render-block at play.html:16-17 is ~0 ms. The cost is a COLD FIRST VISIT cost. That still matters — the project's own testing workflow is a QR scan to a fresh URL, which is exactly the uncontrolled-first-navigation case — but the claim should be scoped to "first visit", not "every launch".

(2) STRONGER THAN STATED — blocking on config.js buys literally nothing: config.js sets gameUrl: "game.html", byte-identical to the fallback already hardcoded at play.html:102. A render-blocking script gates the iframe on a value it never changes. Deleting the tag and keeping the fallback is a zero-risk change.

(3) RECOMMENDATION (2) IS UNSAFE AS WRITTEN — putting src="game.html" in the markup and "appending the query with a tiny inline snippet" means reassigning .src, which re-navigates the iframe and re-downloads a 1.86 MB document. play.html:103-105 explicitly documents that query forwarding (?fresh, ?guest, ?dev, ?qa — and per house rule ?mute) was a real bug: without it a "fresh beginner test was never actually fresh". Do not adopt (2). Adopt (1) + (3) only.

(4) RECOMMENDATION (4) IS A REGRESSION RISK — <link rel="prefetch" as="document" href="game.html"> on index.html pushes 1.86 MB (plus the 1.87 MB logo.png it pulls) onto every homepage visitor including mobile testers who never click. preconnect is fine; the prefetch should be gated on hover/pointerdown/intersection of the Enter button, not unconditional.

SEVERITY — P1 for the finding as a whole is fair, but the weight belongs to the nested-embed defect (a redundant play-bar and a homepage-inside-the-iframe link shown to every tester who uses the primary on-page CTA), not to the millisecond math. The orchestration overhead in isolation is P2; the dominant latency is payload (1.86 MB game.html + 1.87 MB logo.png), which this finding does not address. Effort for the two safe fixes (inline play.html's ~1 KB of used CSS + the --green var and .modal/.btn rules the install modal needs, drop the config.js tag, point index.html:1356 data-game at "game.html") is S. Note index.html:1997-2005 already supplies its own loader and a 15 s error fallback for the embed, so nothing in play.html's bar is needed on that path.

title: The "real markets" section shows a snapshot baked four weeks ago, and mk-fallback cannot detect staleness
evidence: `/* ChartQuest — real daily OHLC snapshot (Yahoo Finance), baked 2026-07-10. */` — today is 2026-08-04. The data ships `{n:"Bitcoin",t:"BTC/USD",...,last:64274.0,chg:-19.8,...}` with candles ending mid-July. Directly above it the page says "Millions of people are buying and selling right now. title: The always-on background FX layer is exempt from the offscreen pause and is never reduced on mobile
evidence: `<div class="worldbg" aria-hidden="true">` has NO `data-fx` attribute, while the pause observer only targets `document.querySelectorAll('[data-fx]')` (index.html:2032) — the four tagged sections are hero/bridge/markets/scroll (verified: `data-fx` appears 7 times, none on worldbg). `.worldbg{position:fixed;inset:0}` (index.html:100) therefore animates for the entire session: 3 `.stream` (index.html:1114-1116, `streamMove`), 6 `.mote` + 3 `.spark` + 2 `.frag` (index.html:1118-1129), and `.wfog` (index.html:1131) = 15 concurrently animating elements. Under them sits `.grain{position:absolute;inset:-50%;mix-blend-mode:overlay}` (index.html:491) — a 4x-viewport-area SVG turbulence layer composited with a blend mode — plus `.nav{position:sticky;backdrop-filter:blur(16px)}` (index.html:155). The ONLY mobile FX reduction in the whole file is `@media (max-width:720px){.ha-glints,.ha-orbit i{display:none}}` (index.html:805).
why: On first paint a phone is compositing three stacked full-viewport layers with two mix-blend-modes plus a blurred sticky nav, while ~23 elements animate (15 worldbg + ha-rays + ha-fog + 6 embers). Every one of those survives scrolling because worldbg is fixed and unpausable. On a mid-range Android this shows up as scroll jank and a warm phone during the exact 30 seconds you need the tester excited enough to tap Play — and battery drain is the top reason a phone tester abandons a browser game. The architecture for fixing this already exists and worldbg was simply left out of it.
recommendation: Two changes, both small. (1) Add `data-fx="world"` to index.html:1089 so the existing `.fx-off` pause (index.html:772) can reach it — though since it is `position:fixed` it is always intersecting, so also (2) add a mobile budget: `@media (max-width:720px){.worldbg .motes,.worldbg .streams,.worldbg .grain{display:none}}`. The `.glow`, `.grid` and `.skyline` are static and carry the whole look; the motes and grain are the invisible-on-a-6-inch-screen part that costs the frames.
